name: Trey Carlisle
role: Program Director; Black Legacy Project Co-Director
contribution: Trey Carlisle is Program Director at Music In Common and Co-Director of the Black Legacy Project. His work brings musicians and communities together through music, storytelling and dialogue across cultural divides.
conversation: Connecting with Mahmood to explore their work as musicians, building bridges across cultures and possibilities for collaboration. An introductory conversation is being arranged.

name: Kenneth Lampl
contribution: Kenneth Lampl is a composer whose work spans film, orchestral music and popular music. His career includes orchestral collaborations involving Foreigner, Evanescence and Radiohead.
conversation: A conversation about film music, orchestras, composition, improvisation and the art of musical storytelling.

name: Gemma Cadwallader
contribution: Gemma works at the intersection of brand storytelling, sponsorship and creative communications.
Her work offers a fascinating perspective on how established songs can bring emotion, familiarity and meaning to visual storytelling.
conversation: The music behind Allianz campaigns, including songs by Sia and Avril Lavigne, and the relationship between popular music and advertising.

name: Sally Beard
contribution: Sally Beard founded Backpacks 4 Vic Kids, an organisation supporting vulnerable children by providing essential belongings and practical assistance during difficult transitions.
Her work demonstrates how a community initiative can grow into meaningful support for children and families.
conversation: The human stories behind Backpacks 4 Vic Kids and the power of community contribution.

name: Dr Janet Hunt
contribution: Dr Janet Hunt's work explores Indigenous community governance, development, social policy and the importance of community leadership.
Her research examines how communities shape their own futures and how institutions can better understand their priorities.
conversation: Community, cultural identity, Indigenous governance and the experiences that shape people's lives.

name: Professor David Shirley
organisation: Western Australian Academy of Performing Arts (WAAPA), Edith Cowan University
contribution: Professor David Shirley is a performing arts educator and academic leader whose work contributes to the development of performers, artists and creative education.
conversation: Artistic identity, performing arts education, creative expression and the future of young performers.
